subject: Economics
description: Article 280, devolution, horizontal and vertical transfers, 15th FC recommendations

questions.stem: The Finance Commission of India is a constitutional body established under:
questions.explanation: Article 280 — the President shall, within two years of the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year (or earlier as required), constitute a Finance Commission. Chairman + 4 other members, appointed by the President. Its job: recommend distribution of net tax proceeds between Centre and States (vertical) and among States (horizontal). First FC in 1951 under K.C. Neogy.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Chairman of the 15th Finance Commission (which covered 2020-21 to 2025-26) was:
questions.explanation: N.K. Singh (former Bihar MP, ex-Revenue Secretary) chaired the 15th FC (2017-21). Its award covered FY 2020-21 initially, then extended to 2021-26 (six years). Reddy — 14th FC; Rangarajan — 12th FC; Kelkar — 13th FC. 16th Finance Commission was constituted in Dec 2023 under Arvind Panagariya (covers 2026-27 to 2030-31). Report due by 31 Oct 2025, implementation 1 Apr 2026.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The 15th Finance Commission recommended that States' share in the net divisible pool of Central taxes be:
questions.explanation: 15th FC kept the vertical devolution at 41% (down from 14th FC's 42%, the 1 percentage point diverted to compensate for J&K losing Statehood and becoming two UTs — Centre retains the share for those UT budgets). This is higher than 13th FC (32%) and 14th FC (42%). 'Vertical' = Centre-vs-States split; 'Horizontal' = inter-State formula weighting population, area, income distance, forest cover, tax effort, demographic performance.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which factor was introduced for the first time in the 15th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula?
questions.explanation: 'Demographic performance' — a reward for lower total fertility rate — was a new 12.5% weight introduced in 15th FC. It compensates southern States for controlling their population (which otherwise lowers their share when population weight is based on latest Census). 15th FC weights: Income distance 45%, Population (2011) 15%, Area 15%, Demographic performance 12.5%, Forest cover 10%, Tax effort 2.5%.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission, constituted in December 2023, is:
questions.explanation: Dr. Arvind Panagariya — economist, former NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman (2015-17), Columbia professor — chairs the 16th FC. Members include Ajay Narayan Jha, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda (econ), Soumya Kanti Ghosh (part-time). Terms of Reference announced 29 Nov 2023. Report to cover five years starting 1 April 2026. Report due 31 Oct 2025.

questions.stem: Under the Constitution, a Finance Commission's recommendations are:

options.option_text: Subject to approval by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: FC recommendations are NOT legally binding. The President lays the FC report before Parliament along with an 'Action Taken Report' explaining which recommendations are accepted. In practice, the Centre has accepted the vertical devolution formula (States' share %) and most grants recommendations from the 11th FC onwards. Grants-in-aid to States under Article 275 and devolution under Article 270 are the two main channels.

questions.stem: The difference between the Finance Commission and the GST Council is that:

options.option_text: FC recommends; GST Council's decisions are binding after notification
Both are binding on Centre and States
FC is statutory; GST Council is constitutional

questions.explanation: FC (Art 280) — constitutional, recommendatory. GST Council (Art 279A, 101st Amendment, 2017) — constitutional and 'recommendatory' on paper, but Supreme Court in Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022) confirmed its recommendations are not binding on Parliament or State legislatures — they act as guidance. However, once accepted and notified, CGST/SGST rates are legally enforced. FC deals with revenue sharing; GST Council deals with tax rates + procedure.
